title: Yara and the Asset
premise: Sable Eastwick's voiceprint unlocks a black-site server in Geneva, exposing 'Asset Yara'—a child witness whose testimony could topple a trilateral arms pact—just days before a global summit. Hunted by three governments' deniable operators and a meticulous assassin named Corven, Sable goes off-grid with the girl she was hired to erase, discovering the client who betrayed her is the mentor who built her career on lies. In a climax inside the summit's secure annex, Sable trades her own fabricated identity as evidence, burning her cover to put Yara's truth on the record. Corven, ordered to silence them both, instead verifies the data and walks away, and Sable survives stripped of her old life but holding something she never had: a family she chose.
about_author: Hazel Thornbury is a former risk analyst who traded briefing rooms for fiction after a decade of redacted documents left her hungry for the whole truth. She writes thrillers about people who keep secrets for a living, from a farmhouse where the nearest neighbor is a locked barn.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine protection detail in Lisbon unravels when her client's phone pings with her own voiceprint authorizing a server she's never touched. She pockets the drive, packs her go-bag out of habit, and feels the first hairline crack in the lie she's lived for ten years. Beat: unease dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Sable traces the authorization to Geneva, where a dead contractor's cold-storage server greets her by name and plays a child's recorded testimony. The file names her employer, Halvorsen Group, as the pact's cleanup crew. She copies everything, knowing copying is a death sentence. Beat: vertigo—her identity is a tool someone else built.

chapters.title: Asset Yara
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introduces Yara, eleven, held in a 'protective residence' outside Bern, rehearsing a retraction she's been coached to give. She memorizes exits the way other children memorize songs. A kind guard slips her a paperclip. Beat: quiet, ferocious hope.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Halvorsen offers her the summit contract: extract Yara, deliver her to the retraction. Sable accepts to get inside, planning the opposite. Her handler, Merrick—her mentor—studies her a beat too long. Beat: the thrill and terror of playing double from the inside.

chapters.title: Bern
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Reconnaissance of the residence reveals Corven's signature: a caretaker already replaced, cameras angled by someone patient. Sable realizes she isn't the only predator circling. She moves her timeline up. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Paperclip
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The extraction goes wrong in the best way: Sable's quiet entry trips an alarm Corven rigged, forcing a fire-escape improvisation. Yara doesn't scream; she navigates. In the getaway car, two liars size each other up and, cautiously, decide to be honest about being liars. Beat: the first stitch of trust.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A border stop proves all three governments have flagged them—someone shared her face across lines that never share anything. She burns her primary identity in a rest-stop dumpster and grieves it more than she expected. Beat: the price of survival, itemized.

chapters.title: The Retraction
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reveals she was made to record a retraction and can recite it perfectly—then recites the truth underneath it instead, showing Sable the coached script's tells. Sable realizes the summit isn't a deadline; it's the only stage where the truth can't be quietly buried. Beat: Yara stops being cargo and becomes the mission's author.

chapters.title: Corven
chapters.summary: Corven's POV, first time. A professional's audit of the failed Bern job, and of Sable: her patterns, her tells, the mentor who trained them both from the same playbook. Corven requests one change to his contract—no deadline extension. He wants this finished cleanly. Beat: dread as craftsmanship.

chapters.title: Merrick
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A dead-drop meeting where Merrick offers her a way back: deliver Yara, keep her name, retire comfortable. Sable hears the offer he once made her at twenty-three, when he rebuilt her from a witness into a weapon. She declines. Beat: the mentor revealed as architect of her cage.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Three days in a farmhouse safehouse: drills, bad soup, a deck of cards, Yara teaching Sable her mother's lullaby in exchange for lock-picking lessons. Found family takes shape in small domestic rituals neither will name. Beat: warmth that raises the stakes.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Geneva files go half-public via an unknown intermediary—enough to panic the pact, not enough to prove. Sable realizes someone is using them as leverage, and Corven uses the chaos to find the farmhouse. They run with minutes to spare. Beat: the world closing in.

chapters.title: Interchange
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. A train-station hunt told as pure procedure—sightlines, timetables, a dropped glove—ending with Corven letting them slip on purpose, disturbed by a discrepancy: the retraction's audio is edited, and his own voice is on the original. Beat: the assassin's certainty cracks.

chapters.title: What Yara Saw
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara finally tells the whole testimony: she witnessed the pact's architects order the strike that killed her family, and Merrick was in the room. Sable understands why Merrick built her—he needed a witness-shaped tool that would never testify. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable approaches a disgraced treaty auditor, Ines Okafor, the only person with summit-annex access and nothing left to lose. The price: Sable's own records—every job, every sanitized incident—as corroborating evidence. She signs. Beat: choosing the truth over the self.

chapters.title: Corven Calls
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, a phone call between Sable and Corven. He offers a trade: Merrick's location for Yara. Sable counters with the edited audio—Corven isn't a hired blade; he's a loose end being tied. Silence, then: 'The annex. I'll be the one you don't see.' Beat: enemies negotiating the shape of a betrayal.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Infiltration of the summit's secure annex with Okafor's credentials while three governments' security details and one assassin share the same corridors. Yara insists on coming; Sable, for the first time, doesn't treat her as someone to hide. Beat: the calm before the break.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara delivers her testimony to Okafor's recorder as alarms cascade—Merrick has triggered a facility lockdown to bury the room. Corven appears not to kill but to authenticate, playing the unedited audio with his own voice in it. Beat: the truth gets its witnesses.

chapters.title: Merrick's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Confrontation with Merrick among locked doors: he offers her everything one last time, then the gun. Sable doesn't outdraw him—she lets him incriminate himself on the live feed, and Corven's single, surgical intervention ends it. Beat: the mentor's fall, and Sable's refusal to become him.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The pact collapses in committee; the three governments scramble to disown deniable assets, including her. Okafor's leak makes Yara's testimony unkillable. Sable is officially erased—which, she realizes, is the first honest thing her file has ever said. Beat: liberation disguised as loss.

chapters.title: Corven's Verdict
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. Corven files a final report exonerating the target and burning his own contract trail, then disappears into a life with no client list. A last scene: he leaves Yara's paperclip, recovered from Bern, on Okafor's desk. Beat: a killer's quiet penance.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Bag
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. Months later, a rented house near the sea: Yara doing homework badly, Okafor visiting with case files, Sable unpacking the go-bag for the first time in ten years and finding nothing in it she needs. Her phone rings with work; she lets it ring. Beat: survival's true price paid, and the family it bought.
